steps.content: When you enter the interrogation room, Mira has just finished telling a WhiteSands joke, and the smiles have yet to fade from the two staff members beside her.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh my... I got so caught up that I lost track of time. Is it already time for our appointment?
Mira turns to you with the perfect amount of surprise and apology on her face. As she moves, you notice the edge of a bandage around her shoulder peeking out from beneath her collar.
I apologize for asking you to do this before your wounds have healed.
However, I need your help to clear some doubts about the recent smuggling case.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Don't worry about it. I wasn't that badly injured. Consider me almost fully recovered after the past few days of rest.
As Mira speaks, she smooths out the creases in her collar so that it covers the bandage. Then, she gives you a reassuring smile.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: So, what would you like to know from me?
At your gesture, the staff leave the interrogation room. Mira leans back casually in her chair, smiling gently as she quietly waits for your questions.
You decide to start with what matters to her most.
As I promised you before, while you were recuperating here, we returned to Tuco and brought your parents to DisCity. They've been admitted to the hospital for specialized treatment.
After initial diagnosis, the doctors believe there's a possibility of recovery.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Really...? That's wonderful!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: When the others at the Bureau told me this, I couldn't quite believe it, but hearing it from you puts my mind completely at ease... Chief, you indeed deserve my trust. I'm glad I placed my bet on you.
You do not respond to her seemingly flattering remarks, and simply continue with a smile.
Sounds like you've really settled in. Getting along well with everyone?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh, yeah... It's really just because everyone here is so kind and helpful. It's not like me doing anything special.
You're well aware of her ability to make people lower their guard. In just a few days, she has won over many at the Bureau with her gentle demeanor and social finesse.
Now, the smile she shows you is one with an endearing mix of modesty and shyness.
But having encountered the unexpected situations during your return to the town and analyzed the entire incident, you no longer look at this seemingly fragile and innocent motel keeper the same way.
That's why you remain unmoved by her display and go on as you've planned.
Besides your parents, we also brought back that smuggling suspect. Despite a head injury, he was lucid enough to confess to smuggling Hypercubes alone, with all the details matching up the records.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh, that's wonderful news. Congrats!
Aren't you surprised?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...Why would I be?
Because he is still alive.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Of course he's alive. I never said he was dead. Chief, are you perhaps misunderstanding something?
Mira gives you a good-natured smile, her tone sincere yet tinged with craftiness.
Then what did you mean by getting rid of him?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: When we're done milking these cash cows dry, we usually sell them off to do manual labor. You know, digging up cacti under the sun on a 140-degree day and stuff.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Those are no good folks anyway. They had it coming. Selling them off brings extra profit for us.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: As for why this one hadn't been shipped off yet... I suppose it's because you arrived too soon, Chief. They hadn't gotten around to it.
What about Tuco? Tell me, how did you manage to make an entire town vanish overnight?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh... Haven't I told you about that already?
At your question, Mira widens her eyes and covers her mouth with her hand somewhat dramatically.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: All the houses in Tuco were built with detachable wooden panels, with sand ships hidden underneath. They were built that way so we can pack up and vanish whenever we need to.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: It was my friend's idea. When you're dealing with either sandstorms or desert bandits every single day, it's really quite a practical solution.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh... I must have forgotten to tell you about that. How careless of me!
Mira gives you an innocent wink, but there isn't a trace of remorse in her voice. Her dismissive attitude annoys you slightly.
I suspect there's quite a bit more you've forgotten to tell me. Would you like me to refresh your memory?
You were far more than a coerced accomplice in Tuco, Mira. At least in this incident, you were the real mastermind behind it all.
This time, Mira doesn't look surprised anymore. She merely narrows her eyes, watching you with keen interest.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: What makes you think that?

You kept insisting that the townsfolks forced you to participate in their scam by threatening your parents' lives. But when we left, you abandoned them in the basement. Weren't you worried about what might happen to them when your betrayal came to light?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The IV could still last for two to three more days, and I'm the only one who knows how to operate the basement's mechanism. No one else could get in.

If that was the case, why did we leave in the first place? If the townsfolks couldn't get in, and I had already agreed to your terms, wouldn't waiting for rescue in the basement have been a safer and wiser choice?
You made the situation sound so urgent that I barely had time to think. I overlooked that, I have to admit.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Chief, don't forget that I took a bullet for you. If I really were the mastermind, why would the townsfolks shoot at us?
I'm afraid that's also part of your plan.
You speak coldly as you produce Mira's special power assessment report.

Your power greatly enhances your strength and reaction speed, allowing you to predict a bullet's trajectory. So when you decided to take that shot for me, you'd already made sure it wouldn't cause a critical injury.
You really went to extraordinary lengths to earn my trust with that performance.
In the brief silence, you lock eyes with Mira, waiting for her response.
Just as you expected, a moment later, Mira begins clapping slowly and lets out a soft laugh, like a cunning little fox.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: All right, all right. Since you're already making such a bold accusation, I guess there's no point in keeping up the act anymore.
She says, giving you an approving nod.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Yes, the townsfolks have never threatened me with my parents. And I've never felt any disgust or weariness toward scamming for a living. As for this plan to steal the Hypercubes, I indeed played the biggest part in it.

options: Ask why she let you off

choices.text: Ask why she let you off

steps.content: But that would mean you and the people of Tuco were in this together. There would have been no reason for you to escape.
So why did you change your mind and let me go? What other plans did you guys have?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Our only plan...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...is to escape. To let the whole town of Tuco escape.
She lowers her eyes, her smile unchanged yet somehow taking on a cold edge.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Be grateful your position saved you from a grim fate, Chief.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If we'd seriously crossed someone of your status, the bigwigs of DisCity like you wouldn't have let Tuco off easily. You guys would have wiped Tuco out like brushing away a grain of sand.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: So I changed my plan and decided to let you go, so you'd owe me a favor.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...And of course, that alone wouldn't have been enough.
Mira's lips curl into a knowing smile.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I needed to mix lies into truth to earn your sympathy and trust, making you willingly play into my new plan.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Like telling you the truth about my past and my parents. Like risking my life to take that bullet for you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: This way, you would choose to retreat, buying time for everyone in Tuco to escape. And the heavy sandstorm that night was perfect for concealing the sand ships' tracks.
We had only known each other for less than a day then. How were you so certain I wouldn't go back to clear out the town first?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You wouldn't. Because you have a conscience. It's the easiest quality to spot in a person, and I saw it in you right away.
Mira is smiling cunningly again. You recall that back in Tuco, this charming lady was always one step ahead of your thoughts.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I tried hard, Chief, to make you believe I was gravely wounded while saving you, and that there were people in danger desperately needing those Hypercubes. That guilty conscience behind these beliefs drives your next move, stronger than any other emotion.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I'm truly sorry, but I did use you for my own ends.
Her smile carries an unbothered ease unusual for her young age. You can't really tell if it contains more remorse for tricking you or smugness from succeeding in doing so.
Your plan certainly worked this time. With your help, everyone in Tuco evaded our capture.
But what about next time?
Mira fixes you with an enigmatic smile.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Is that a threat, Chief? Just because you have me, the mastermind, under control doesn't mean Tuco will be left helpless and surrender easily. Tuco has a good leader. It's no easy prey for you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Unless the leader comes to you personally, you won't find even a single trace of Tuco.
Leader? Is that the friend you mentioned earlier, the one who hid sand ships under the houses?
She answers with only a smile, clearly not intending to reveal anything more.
You remain unfazed, turning instead to the investigation report received today. It details several cases allegedly involving Tuco and the evacuation route confirmed by thorough on-site analysis.
No matter how capable this leader of yours might be, I doubt she could stand against the FAC and the MBCC alone.
Based on the evidence we've gathered, there are substantial grounds to suspect Tuco's involvement in several unsolved Hypercube smuggling cases.
Stealing strategic resources, disrupting official trade... neither of these are minor offenses.
With the FAC's force and intelligence network, it's only a matter of time before we pinpoint their location again.
Her expression freezes for a moment as she stares at the report in your hand. But she quickly regains her composure and speaks firmly, though her speech has noticeably quickened.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You're not going to do it, Chief. You're just bluffing.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The Hypercubes have been retrieved and the case is closed. You must have more important matters to attend to than pursuing a bunch of harmless small-time scammers like us.
Sorry but that's merely your own speculation.
As the Chief of Minos, I'm responsible for DisCity's safety too. Mira, perhaps you don't know me as well as you think you do.
The interrogation room falls into complete silence.
The gentle smile slowly fades from Mira's face. For the first time, you see clear hostility in her icy gaze.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...By DisCity's laws, Tuco has indeed committed many crimes, and this wasn't the first time we'd scammed smugglers either.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But why should we play by your rules?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: WhiteSands isn't DisCity. We don't get to live comfortably by monopolizing Hypercubes. To survive in the desert, we must become the most ruthless and powerful predator. That's the law of survival in WhiteSands.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Were those "victims" truly innocent? What happened to my parents wasn't an isolated incident. These desert bandits and smugglers have ruined countless lives.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Tuco is merely acting in self-defense. Those who commit atrocities and drive others into the dead-end of life, are the ones who should be arrested and held accountable.
She gives you a faint mocking smile.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Or, does the honorable and righteous DisCity only dare to prey on easy targets like us?
Ignoring her blatant provocation, you simply point to the section about the treatment of the Hypercubes in the document.
Take a look at this.

The Hypercubes that Tuco stole for its survival were also vital to other bases and shelters in WhiteSands. It looks like your self-defense might also be built on indirectly harming other innocent people.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But we didn't know about this before, and the smugglers are the root cause of all this. Tuco isn't the real culprit!

That doesn't change the fact that you were involved in it, and DisCity authorities cannot turn a blind eye to this. The turmoil in WhiteSands has persisted far too long with severe consequences. We will take immediate action to...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Enough! Save your fancy talk! I don't want to hear it!
Your condescending attitude enrages her. Mira bursts out in anger.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Have any of you pampered DisCity elites ever truly cared about the lives in WhiteSands?!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The "turmoil in Whitesands"? "Immediate action"? But the truth is you only care when your own interests are at stake!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: And you've never done anything more than chasing the smugglers away and setting up barriers. There's never been any real arrest or control.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: And after driving these criminals into WhiteSands, you even began targeting the ordinary people of WhiteSands who were already struggling to survive!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You've protected your interests, but what about us?
She glares at you with an intense gaze that carries both sorrow and disappointment.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, the renowned new Chief of Minos, your great achievements have reached even us in WhiteSands, and we've all been in awe.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: A while ago, we happened to meet a young Syndican girl from Minos. She'd been through hard times too, but whenever she spoke of you, she was filled with trust and pride, as if you were the most remarkable person in the world to her.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: That's why I thought you might be different from those condescending officials, that maybe you would understand. That's why I decided to leave with you and even entrust my parents' life to you...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But now I see, I was just being naive.
Mira slumps back in her chair, and silence falls over the interrogation room, just like when you had that conversation in the dark.
Mira, I'm glad you've shared your true feelings. But before you lose faith in me completely, please let me finish.
You take a deep breath and clear your throat.
I'm well aware of these problems too, which is why I've  already assigned more forces to capture these roaming desert bandits and smugglers, just a few days ago.
Do you think this will work, Mira?
The unexpected words clearly catch Mira off guard. Confusion flashes across her face before she quickly composes herself, narrowing her eyes with a mix of resignation and reproach.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...Chief, I didn't take you as the type to tease. So were you just trying to get back to me by scaring me? Bravo, even I couldn't tell whether you're being serious or not.
Well, now you get a taste of your own medicine.
You set aside the Tuco investigation report and drop the playful tone, restating your stance seriously.
As a DisCity official, I must say certain correct words, as required by my job. But as you pointed out earlier, this kind of rigid correctness doesn't always apply to every situation.
It's easy to judge with an absolute right or wrong, but doing so to those struggling to survive hardships without having gone through them yourself, is nothing but arrogant and cruel.
While my duties require me to judge your actions, I agree with you that there should be a proper order of priority in how we handle this.

Compared to those struggling to survive, it's the desert bandits and smugglers who sowed this in the first place, and that should be our primary targets. This should be the true purpose of my duty to judge.
You look at Mira sitting across from you. She's lowered her head, hiding her reaction. For a moment, you can only hear her breathing in the interrogation room.

Then, she raises her head and smiles at you. It's the first time you've seen a smile carrying this kind of emotion on her face. It's pure and refreshing like a spring in the desert. You know this is a genuine smile from Mira.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...Chief, I'm truly glad to hear that from you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If you like, I'm willing to do whatever I can to help you catch those bastards in WhiteSands. After all, I'm one of the Bureau's Sinners now. You can find me whenever you want.
Mira's casual remark brings a long-lingering question to your mind.
Being detained by the Bureau means a certain degree of restraint. Mira, when you first planned all this, did you already consider sacrificing your freedom for the people of Tuco?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Sacrifice? I wouldn't really call it a sacrifice.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Look at how things have turned out. You caught the smuggler, retrieved the Hypercubes, and brought back this Sinner who was the "mastermind" that tried to trick you. Your mission is a huge success.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: As for me, my parents now have access to better treatment and proper care, while everyone in Tuco managed to evade capture.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: If I must say what I had in mind when planning this... I guess this is exactly the best win-win situation I hoped for.
Mira gives you a playful wink, seeming optimistic about her arrest and even a bit smug about how things have turned out.
You sigh inwardly. Worried that she hasn't fully grasped her situation, you decide to remind her gently.
I'm not sure if you're aware, but detained Sinners aren't free to leave the Bureau. This means you won't be able to go home, at least for now. Are you really okay with that?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Hmm... for those of us who grew up in the desert, home isn't necessarily a fixed place. Home is where our family is. Since my parents are in DisCity now, this can be my home too.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Besides, I'm not that child who could only run away crying for help anymore. Nope. Now I can thrive anywhere.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: As for Tuco, it's not like I can never go back. I've already asked around in the Bureau. You have a parole system, right? There are quite a few Sinners who already got out.
...I see you've made yourself at home in the Bureau, getting along with everyone and keeping yourself well-informed. That's good. However, parole has special requirements that you don't meet yet.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh? Well, I'll meet them very soon.
She smiles, her tone light but inexplicably sure.
What are you plotting this time?
Your eyes narrow with suspicion, but Mira only returns your gaze innocently as she earnestly defends herself.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Nothing! Chief, I'll surely follow the rules and be on my best behavior in your territory. After all, I'm counting on your approval to let me visit my hometown occasionally.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: It's just... who knows what the future holds. Things happen, right?
Her smile remains gentle and harmless, yet her thoughts beneath remain mysteriously unreadable.
Since she clearly understands her situation and has her future plotted well, there's no need to press further as long as she doesn't break any rules.
Having got the answers to all your questions, you check the time, then carefully take out something you've been carrying with you.
You carefully hand the family photo you retrieved from the basement back to Mira.
I thought this might be important to you? I brought it back with me.
Seeing her eyes light up with joy, you smile and tell her about the second surprise.

Also, I've arranged for your temporary release tomorrow, and I'll accompany you to the hospital. You haven't seen your parents since coming to DisCity, right? It'll put your mind at ease to see them in person.
Thank you. You think that's what she says in that trembling, almost choked voice.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I'm home! Did you miss me while I was away?
In the sunlit hospital room, Mira replaces the photo frame by her parents' bedside.
She sits down on the chair beside them, tenderly fixing her parents' hair and clothes as they lie in bed. Then, she begins with a gentle smile.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...I've missed you two, so much.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Look, we've finally made it to DisCity, together! What a tough journey it was. But at least your wish has come true.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: There are many trees and bustling streets everywhere. At night, the city lights shine brighter than the stars... If only you could open your eyes to see them.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The doctors here say they might be able to cure you. So, wake up, okay? I'm right here waiting for you, not going anywhere.
A lump rises in her throat and tears well in her eyes. Mira takes several deep breaths to force down the surge of emotions, just as she always does.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But don't make me wait too long... please...
She catches a glimpse of the figure waiting patiently outside the hospital room, and a smile finds its way back to her eyes before she notices.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Oh, and you know, I was right about that Chief. Told you, I know a good person when I see one.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I've always trusted my judgment, but I was still worried... What if he went back on his word and refused to bring you back? Thankfully, that didn't happen. Maybe this means I can trust him a little more?
steps.female_content: I've always trusted my judgment, but I was still worried... What if she went back on her word and refused to bring you back? Thankfully, that didn't happen. Maybe this means I can trust her a little more?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I'm doing well at the MBCC under his cover. Everyone back home is doing fine too.
steps.female_content: I'm doing well at the MBCC under her cover. Everyone back home is doing fine too.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: He says I can visit the desert whenever I miss it. I should take him with me next time! You should've seen him when he first came to Tuco. We gave him quite a scare! But we haven't shown him real desert hospitality yet!
steps.female_content: She says I can visit the desert whenever I miss it. I should take her with me next time! You should've seen her when she first came to Tuco. We gave her quite a scare! But we haven't shown her real desert hospitality yet!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I wonder if he'll sing and dance at the bonfire fest...
steps.female_content: I wonder if she'll sing and dance with us at the bonfire fest...

steps.content: A sudden breeze sweeps through the treetops outside the hospital window.
The leaves rustle softly, like words filled with longing from a distance, too soft to be heard, responding to the girl: They are listening.
